verdict.rationale:
Homebrew's docs clearly document third-party taps (`brew tap`/`untap`) as add-on repositories for formulae, casks and external commands, plus a Bundler system that can drive non-Homebrew backends (npm, cargo, uv, Krew, WinGet, Flatpak, etc.), showing broad plugin/backend extensibility. One community report notes that self-hosting a tap is harder than a standard apt/yum repo, a minor friction point but not a functional failure.

missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification of writing a custom external command or plugin beyond docs, and more than one community data point on tap ecosystem health.
